title: Land-Equity Allowance in Operating Lines of Credit Shortfall Paydowns
content:
Equity a member holds in farmland mortgaged to the association counts in the member's favour when an Operating Lines of Credit line is brought back within its borrowing base. The allowance turns on the member's Farm Real Estate Loans.

## Rule

A land-equity allowance is taken off the shortfall:

- **1.0 percent of the line's commitment** when the member holds a Farm Real Estate loan in active status whose mortgaged collateral value less its principal balance is at least 0.5 of the commitment;
- **0.5 percent of the commitment** when that land equity is at least 0.25 of the commitment but below 0.5 of it;
- **nothing** when the member holds no Farm Real Estate loan in active status, or its land equity is below 0.25 of the commitment.

Land equity is the loan's mortgaged collateral value less its principal balance, as the member's Farm Real Estate Loans records show. The allowance is subtracted from the shortfall — the outstanding principal less the limit it is measured against — and what remains is never less than zero.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical operating line, commitment USD 2,000,000)

| Farm Real Estate loan in active status | Collateral value | Principal balance | Land equity | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Held | USD 2,600,000 | USD 1,600,000 | USD 1,000,000 (0.5 of the commitment) | USD 20,000 (1.0%) |
| Held | USD 2,600,000 | USD 1,600,001 | USD 999,999 | USD 10,000 (0.5%) |
| Held | USD 1,500,000 | USD 1,000,000 | USD 500,000 (0.25 of the commitment) | USD 10,000 (0.5%) |
| Held | USD 1,500,000 | USD 1,000,001 | USD 499,999 | Nothing |
| None in active status | — | — | — | Nothing |
